title: Deterministic action IDs and offload hinting — PRD draft
summary: Draft spec for a deterministic action-id scheme plus lightweight offload hints to make streaming tool-calls and structured outputs replayable, resumable, and more cache/edge-friendly without heavy client changes.
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a simple deterministic action-id contract and an "offload_hint" field that clients and the hosted runtime can use to: 1) deterministically identify granular tool calls and structured output frames across retries/stream reconnects; 2) communicate cheap op-level hints for placement/caching/offload to edge SDKs and routing; 3) allow resumable, replayable sessions without forcing full session snapshot uploads.

Motivation / problems we see in the wild
- SDKs and clients reconnecting mid-stream often produce duplicate tool calls or lose idempotency because tool boundaries have no stable identifiers.
- Fallbacks (e.g., cheap model variant to expensive model) create divergent tooling interactions that are hard to reconcile on resume.
- Edge proxies and mobile SDKs want to make placement decisions (local simulation, pre-warm, route to dedicated pool) but lack a lightweight signals surface.
- Current streaming frames are opaque for caching and partial-reuse — we want to make small, safe additions to enable more robust UX without breaking existing contracts.

Design principles
- Backwards compatible: default values must preserve current behavior; new fields are optional.
- Small API surface: one stable per-tool-call id + a tiny hint enum.
- Deterministic: IDs can be generated by client or server but have canonical form so both can agree after reconnect.
- Safe to expose: IDs/hints must not leak sensitive material.

Goals
- Reduce duplicate tool invocations after reconnects by 80% for common failure profiles.
- Enable client-side resume with minimal state: a short ledger of last N action IDs + their intended semantics.
- Allow edge SDKs to make placement decisions with >60% accuracy for pre-warm/offload heuristics on initial request.

Non-goals
- Not a replacement for full session checkpointing.
- Not an authorization mechanism for tool access.

Key concepts
1) action_id (string)
- A short, deterministic identifier assigned to each logical tool call or action frame.
- Format suggestion (human-friendly and collision resistant): <client_ns>~<monotonic_counter>~<crc4>
  - client_ns: optional short client namespace (alphanumeric, 6 chars max) or server-generated ns
  - monotonic_counter: client-maintained increment (numeric) or server-supplied sequence
  - crc4: 4 hex chars for cheap accidental duplication detection
- Examples: "cliA1~17~a3f2", "srv~1024~1b9c"
- Generation: client preferred (to keep deterministic across retries); server assigns if absent and echoes back in frames.

2) offload_hint (enum string) — optional
- Purpose: micro-hint to runtime/edge to prefer certain placements or modes for the tool invocation without affecting semantics.
- Allowed values (initial set): "local-simulate", "prewarm", "dedicated-route", "best-effort-cache", "no-offload"
- Semantics:
  - local-simulate: client-side SDK may simulate a deterministic outcome locally for latency-sensitive UIs; runtime must still execute the canonical call and reconcile if mismatch.
  - prewarm: try to warm the tool or model variant early (useful for heavy cold-start tools)
  - dedicated-route: prefer Dedicated capacity pools when available (useful for latency-critical tool calls)
  - best-effort-cache: allow the runtime to reply from cached results if deterministic (e.g., idempotent data lookup)
  - no-offload: explicitly disable any proxy/edge offload for sensitive calls

3) action_frame object (stream semantics)
- Each streaming frame that marks a completed tool call or structured output block should include: action_id, action_type (tool name or "structured-output"), status (started|in_progress|complete|error), and optional offload_hint.
- Frames may be sparse; the SDK should be prepared to receive out-of-order frames but the action_id enables reconciliation.

API sketches (HTTP/stream protocol additions)
- request body (initial call) additions (all optional):
  - client_ns: string
  - initial_counter: integer (client-suggested starting monotonic value)
  - action_ledger: [{"action_id":string, "status":string}] (small list for resume hints)
- streaming frames (server->client) additions: in each frame envelope attach any of:
  - action_id: string
  - action_type: string
  - offload_hint: string
  - canonical: boolean (server asserts canonical id if assigned)
- example minimal JSON frame: {"seq": 431, "action_id": "cliA1~17~a3f2", "action_type": "lookup-weather", "status": "complete", "offload_hint": "best-effort-cache"}

SDK ergonomics and migration guidance
- Minimal changes for clients:
  - When initiating calls, client MAY provide a client_ns and initial_counter if it intends to generate deterministic action_ids.
  - For each tool call, client generates action_id using its monotonic counter and includes it in the call envelope.
  - Maintain a tiny ring-buffer ledger of last ~32 action_ids and statuses; send this ledger on reconnects in the action_ledger field to aid server reconciliation.
- Mobile and JavaScript SDKs:
  - Expose a convenience helper: newActionId(client_ns) which returns the formatted id and increments an internal counter stored in memory (not persisted by default).
  - Provide an opt-in persistent ledger mode for apps that want full resume across app restarts (store the ring-buffer in secure storage).

Server/runtime behavior (recommendations)
- When a request arrives with client action_id fields:
  - Validate format and case-insensitive uniqueness within session.
  - If duplicate action_id already executed to completion in session history, return the existing result instead of re-executing (idempotent fast-path), unless offload_hint=="no-offload" or tool-level policy forbids caching.
  - If the server assigns an action_id (client omitted), mark it canonical:true on the frames so clients can persist it for resume.
- Offload_hint handling:
  - Hints are advisory only. The runtime may ignore them based on policy, security, or capacity.
  - Use telemetry to decide heuristics: e.g., if >70% of calls with prewarm succeed with lower P99 after prewarm, promote the hint to an optimization path.

Telemetry and observability
- New telemetry events to emit (each with action_id tag):
  - action.assigned (who assigned id: client|server)
  - action.replayed (server returned cached response for action_id)
  - action.duplicate_detected (client resubmitted same id while in progress)
  - offload.hint_applied (boolean)
  - offload.hint_ignored (reason)
- Dashboard: per-client_ns heatmap, offload hint success rates, percentage of client-generated ids vs server-generated.

Security and privacy notes
- action_id and offload_hint must not carry secrets. They are metadata only.
- Do not store action payloads in any cache unless the tool explicitly declares idempotent/cachable semantics.

Failure and edge cases
- Counter rollover or lost counter: if the client reuses a counter by mistake, server treats it as new unless action_id exact match exists and is within session ledger. Document recommended counter length and advise clients to adopt monotonic counters that survive reconnects for the best experience.
- Out-of-order frames: SDKs must reconcile by action_id, not frame seq. Provide helper utilities to "stitch" partial frames into a final action object.

Concrete examples
- Example: mobile client wants near-instant UX for address lookup tool:
  - client_ns="mAddr", initial_counter=100
  - client calls tool with action_id="mAddr~101~4c1a" and offload_hint="local-simulate"
  - SDK returns a local best-guess UI immediately while the server processes canonical call; when server frame arrives with final verification, SDK reconciles and shows the authoritative result or a small correction.

Open questions and trade-offs
- Should we allow signed action_ids to prevent accidental collisions across misbehaving clients? (trade: heavier crypto vs simplicity)
- Should offload_hint be extensible via a small taxonomy registry so partners can register hints? (trade: managing registry complexity)
- How long to keep per-session action_id history for safe replay semantics without blowing up state? Proposal: keep last 500 ids per session for Dedicated customers and last 100 for hosted-default.

Acceptance criteria (for an initial MVP)
- API additions are optional and do not break existing clients.
- Mobile and JS SDKs expose new helper functions and default ledger of size 32.
- Backend emits telemetry for action.assigned and action.replayed.
- End-to-end test coverage demonstrating resume after a mid-stream disconnect does not re-run idempotent lookup tools more than once in 95% of injected disconnect scenarios.

Next steps / roadmap
- Design review with serving-runtime and SDK teams (1 week).
- Spike: implement server echo of assigned action_id + offload telemetry (2 sprints).
- SDK helpers (mobile/JS/Python) + opt-in persistent ledger (1 sprint).
- Pilot with Solutions Engineering on 2 customers for address lookup and knowledge-base retrieval (1 month).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally conservative: the goal is to unlock better resume and low-risk offload behaviors without a heavy contract change. Feedback: prefer small enums and client-first id generation.

Appendix: quick JSON examples
- Initial request envelope (minimal):
  {
    "prompt": "Find nearby coffee shops",
    "client_ns": "mAddr",
    "initial_counter": 100
  }

- Tool invocation frame (client->server):
  {
    "action_id": "mAddr~101~4c1a",
    "action_type": "kb-lookup",
    "offload_hint": "local-simulate",
    "input": { "query": "coffee near me" }
  }

- Server streaming completion frame (server->client):
  {
    "seq": 203,
    "action_id": "mAddr~101~4c1a",
    "action_type": "kb-lookup",
    "status": "complete",
    "canonical": true,
    "result": { "items": [...] }
  }
